project: GPS Triangle — Bill Maisey performance analysis & coaching report
note: Master feature + testing backlog. TDD applies to the build: for each feature, write a failing test (red), implement to green, then flip passes=true and commit test+impl+spec together. Data/analysis features are validated by reconciliation tests (computed values match the authoritative rcmodelspot results and API distance fields). Scaffold captured 2026-09-27 ahead of build; refine before building.

features.description: Fetch competition standings and heat/group tree for the Oschatz 2026 event from the rcmodelspot JSON API
steps: GET /CompetitionGpsTriangle/Results/{guid} and cache raw JSON
Parse standings (38 pilots) and heats -> groups -> per-flight results
Test: Bill's 17 flights are present and his total (12562) and rank (22) reconcile to the standings

features.description: Fetch per-group ~1Hz GPS replay tracks and select Bill plus the same-air group leader per round
steps: For each of Bill's 17 groups, GET /CompetitionGpsTriangle/ReplayGroup/{groupId}
Identify the scoring flight (handle multi-start artefacts) and the top-scoring same-group leader

Test: Bill and leader tracks present in all 17 groups and leader laps/speed/score reconcile to the results tree (test_data002_bill_and_leader_tracks_present_all_rounds, test_data002_leader_laps_and_speed_reconcile)

Test: the scored start T0 equals the flightStart of the gpsTriangleStats entry the API itself scored, for both pilots in all 17 rounds including the multi-start cases (test_data002_scored_start_matches_api_scored_stats, test_data002_multi_start_rounds_are_present_and_isolated)

features.description: Enrich each flight with weather from the Open-Meteo ERA5 archive at the Oschatz coordinates
steps: GET ERA5 hourly (wind, temp, cloud, radiation, boundary-layer height) for 3-8 Aug 2026, Europe/Berlin. CAPE is requested but the archive returns null for all 144 hours, so it is not carried into the CSVs; boundary-layer height is the secondary thermal proxy
Map each flight's group start time to the nearest hour

Test: every flight's weather hour is its published group start time rounded to the nearest hour, recomputed from results.json and the archive's own utc_offset_seconds, and the joined values equal that ERA5 row (test_data003_every_flight_maps_to_its_own_start_hour, test_data003_weather_values_come_from_the_archive_hour, test_data003_cape_is_null_in_the_archive_and_absent_from_the_csv)

features.description: Per-round metric bundle (laps, avg speed, entry altitude/speed, energy, thermalling, pacing, line efficiency) for Bill vs same-air leader
steps: Compute metrics from tracks; convert units (groundSpeed km/h, vario, haversine distances)
Test: computed laps and avg speed equal the authoritative results for every flight; track-derived lap markers equal the official lap count (test_anl001_track_derived_lap_count_matches_official)

Test: the API's distanceCovered/distance/lapStats fields are all zero, so distances are validated against the API-IMPLIED scoring lap instead - allTrianglesAvgSpeed * timeElapsedSeconds / laps equals the ADR-008 perimeter 350*(2+2*sqrt(2)) = 1689.9 m on all 17 rounds, and the analysis scripts' PERIMETER_M matches it (test_anl001_api_implied_lap_distance_is_the_course_perimeter, test_anl001_perimeter_constants_match_the_adr008_course)

features.description: Flight-phase decomposition (start / straight / turn / climb) with per-lap time-deficit attribution vs leader
steps: Segment tracks by bearing-rate and vario; separate turnpoint turns from thermal circles by duration/continuity
Attribute per-lap deficit across phases; rank phases by cost to Bill

Test: cruise+turn+climb reconstructs each lap time and the lap times sum to the aloft window; speedrun rounds 4/10/16 excluded (test_anl002_phase_times_sum_to_lap_time, test_anl002_lap_times_sum_to_aloft_time, test_anl002_speedrun_rounds_are_excluded)

Test: aloft time equals the API's timeElapsedSeconds on every single-attempt flight; on re-started flights the window spans all logged attempts and is pinned as a known limitation (test_anl002_aloft_time_matches_api_elapsed, test_anl002_multi_start_aloft_spans_all_attempts)

features.description: Condition-dependence analysis: Bill's within-group (conditions-controlled) score vs wind and thermal-strength proxies, and time-of-day
steps: Join weather to per-flight scores; compute associations with n caveat. The normalised-score target is reported twice - over all 17 flights (labelled as such) and over the 14 distance heats alone, since the three one-lap sprints are scored by a different model; the report quotes the distance-only row

Test: the score, laps and speed correlations are available over the 14 distance rounds, the all-17 row stays explicitly labelled, and the radiation association is asserted as a direction and magnitude band rather than a significance claim (test_anl003_distance_only_score_correlations_are_reported, test_anl003_all_17_score_row_is_labelled_as_such, test_anl003_radiation_association_is_positive_and_suggestive, test_anl003_laps_correlations_use_the_14_distance_rounds)

features.description: GPS ground-track chart: the FACTUAL course from the .rct, reconciled with the GPS tracks in ONE consistent equirectangular projection (cos(lat) longitude, identical for course and tracks). GEOMETRY (corrected - it is NOT equilateral): the course is a RIGHT-ISOSCELES triangle - the three turnpoints sit at RADIUS = the .rct 'length' (350 m, NOT the leg) from the start, at bearings {axis, axis+180, axis-90}; the apex is at axis-90 (pointing away from the ground/safety zones - a fixed venue side); the base (hypotenuse, 2xradius = 700 m) runs along the axis with the start at its midpoint; the two legs are radius*sqrt2 (~495 m); perimeter ~1690 m matches the regs lap. Draw the triangle bold, ink, LAST on top with turnpoint dots; the start/finish as a dashed perpendicular line at the start; full-resolution traces at low opacity; North arrow top-right; 100 m scale bar bottom-left; legend inside bottom-right (right-aligned row); wind vector in the margin at the CLOCKFACE position of the wind's source bearing (see RPT-012 - not a fixed right band), with the plot grid/frame sized so the wind arrow sits WITHIN the framed image on whichever side it lands (not outside the grid); legend/scale/North never overlap the wind vector; legend row spacing keeps swatches and labels from overlapping. CAPTION: derive the course geometry from course_geometry() per ADR-008 (350 m turnpoint radius, ~495 m legs, 700 m base, ~1690 m lap) - never describe the 350 m radius as the 'leg' - and derive the wind-position clause from the round's own source bearing rather than hard-coding a side
steps: Per heat parse the .rct T: header (start, axis, radius); turnpoints = start + radius at {axis, axis+180, axis-90}, apex = axis-90; project course and replay identically; render with the orientation aids

Test (both pilots, thermalling excluded): turn-arc radius from start ~ the .rct length (350 m) within ~15%; flown leg bearings match course-leg bearings within a few degrees; each corner's fitted arc centre within a small margin of the course corner with the pilot apex just OUTSIDE; start-crossing centroid at the course start; projected distance between two .rct coords equals their haversine distance; Bill and leader agree; triangle drawn last; North+scale+legend present and clear of the wind vector

features.description: Per-plot wind annotation: on each GPS-trace plot show a wind vector arrow positioned at the clockface location of the wind source bearing, OUTSIDE the trace box, pointing inward (the direction the wind blows), with a compass+degrees label (e.g. WNW 285) and speed in KNOTS beneath; small but legible; dark grey/off-black FIX (v2 bug): the wind glyph must sit at the CLOCKFACE position of the SOURCE bearing on the correct side (W/272 -> LEFT of the traces, E -> right, N -> top, S -> bottom), in the margin outside the traces but inside the framed image (size the frame to include whichever side), with the ARROWHEAD pointing INWARD (the direction the wind blows toward centre). A fixed right-band placement is wrong for non-easterly winds.
steps: Pass per-round wind (dir/speed) to the ground-track chart; place arrow+label at the bearing's clockface position outside the plot; convert km/h to knots; compute the compass point from the bearing
Test: each ground-track plot renders a wind arrow at the correct clockface position with a knots label; northerly does not collide with the North marker

features.description: Per-round view opens (under the summary) with a 'Visual overview of performance' dashboard, then the Energy Management, ground-track and other sections. TOP ROW - four vertical visuals in order: (1) SCORE as a symmetric vertical density/violin of the group field scores in mid-grey, with the winner as a blue line at 1000 and Bill as a green line at his score over the top; (2) ENTRY SPEED, (3) ENTRY ALTITUDE, (4) AVERAGE SPEED (SINGLE-LAP SPEED on speed runs) as BULLET plots - the grey track top is the regs cap where one exists (entry speed 120, entry altitude 400) else a sensible domain max; the leader is a blue line; Bill is the green fill; Bill's value labelled in GREEN to the RIGHT of the bar (not black, not on the bar); NO orange cap line and NO field on the bullets. BOTTOM ROW: LAPS as a small paired bar chart (no axis; value labels on top; Bill green, leader blue); within-group RANK as text (N/field) - relabelled 'Field rank / N pilots in the field' on the three speed rounds, which are scored across the whole 38-pilot field rather than within a heat group; a WIND compass card (arrow at source bearing blowing inward + speed); SOLAR as a relative colour-bar - height proportional to the round's solar normalised across all rounds (lowest round still shows a small bar), each bar a SOLID colour interpolated deep-red at the event max to pastel-yellow at the min, no scale/labels. LEGEND top-right as a colour key with SQUARE swatches: Bill Maisey (green), 'Round Leader (<name>)' with the round leader's actual name (blue), and 'Regs limit / Other pilots' (grey - grey means both the regs cap on bullets and the field on the violin) - this replaces the per-round 'Bill vs leader' header text. Lay the dashboard as a 2-row x 4-column grid with the bottom row (laps/rank/wind/solar) aligned to the top row's columns The dashboard's lead-in text is NOT a description of the panel (it speaks for itself) - it is 3-5 sentences of round-specific KEY INSIGHTS: the salient performance points and how Bill differed from the same-air leader this round (data-grounded), for every round.
steps: Build score-violin, bullet, paired-bar, wind-card and solar-colourbar SVG components; assemble as the first per-round section

Test: renders the score violin (blue 1000 + green Bill over grey field density), four bullets (grey=regs cap or domain, blue leader, green Bill, green value on the right, no orange), a laps paired-bar, rank text, wind card, and a normalised red-to-yellow solar bar; works for triangle and speed rounds

features.description: Overview is organised as an 'Overall Read' lead paragraph (before the sections) + a section index/links near the top, then FOUR Title-Case thematic sections. Within each section insights run top-down general->specific, each as Title -> Insight text -> Visual (+grounding/citations) -> recommendation. SECTIONS: (1) Headline Result: number cards (rank 22/38, total, gap, landings) + Within-Group Rank + Gap Breakdown (waterfall) + Where The Ground Is Lost (phase-lever ranking) + Consistency: Floor vs Ceiling + Progression Across The Week + a Landings strength callout. (2) Scoring, Laps & Speed: Score Per Round -> Laps Per Round -> Cruise Speed -> Field Position & Laps/Speed Scatter -> Speed Gaps. (3) Start Energy: Entry Speed -> Entry Altitude -> Airframe/Equipment note (RPT-025). (4) Conditions, Trajectory & Climbing: Conditions Dependence (Spearman explained in plain English) -> Trajectory Trends (RPT-023) -> Thermal Strength/Weather -> Climb Geometry -> Climb Rate -> Thermalling Turn Radius (RPT-024) -> the Round 12 ground-track embedded as a worked example. ROUND 12 FRAMING (corrected against the data): it is the weak-lift bombout - Bill took 2 laps to the leader's 8, his fastest clean lap covered 4,622 m of ground to the leader's 1,819 m (line ratio 2.54) in off-course loops searching for lift, while turn radii were comparable (42.0 vs 40.9 m). DROP the 'Conditions Link' insight; the old Performance-Summary grouped bars move into these thematic homes. NOTE on the grouped bars: score/laps/avg speed carry all three series, but entry speed and entry altitude carry two (round winner + Bill) - only Bill and each round's same-air winner were track-analysed, so the event winner has no entry telemetry and is stated as absent in the prose. CONDITIONS DEPENDENCE is computed and plotted over the 14 DISTANCE rounds only (the three sprints score on a different task), with the Spearman rho quoted from those same rows.
steps: Build a grouped-bar all-rounds chart component (winner/overall-winner/Bill) and render it for score, laps, avg speed, entry speed, entry altitude; add a conditions strip
Test: Performance summary renders the grouped-bar charts across all rounds with the three series, above the existing Overview content

features.description: Overview 'Trajectory Trends' insight: distance-from-course density, Bill vs round winner, pooled over the 14 distance rounds, LOG-frequency y-axis ONLY (drop the linear panel). Plain-English lead: most flight time is spent lapping on the course line (hence the log y-axis to expose rare far excursions); the winner's distribution is a tight peak against the course line with a long flat tail - he holds most of his flight time within 40 m of a leg yet is willing to stray much further to exploit lift (quantify both tail shares from the same density dict rather than calling the shape 'bimodal', which the plotted density does not show); Bill sits in a moderate mid-band. Extend the log y-axis floor (0.1/0.01/0.001% ...) with a floor so Bill's green line ALWAYS stays above the x-axis (handle zero bins). Unfilled line per pilot; Bill green / winner blue.
